additional_requirements: The binge eating and inappropriate compensatory behaviors both occur, on average, at least once a week for 3 months

S046.name: Body_Image_Weight_Shape_Disturbance
S046.description: Undue influence of body weight or shape on self-evaluation.

subtypes.Distorted Body Image: Perceiving one's body as much fatter than it actually is or perceiving specific parts as excessively large when looking in the mirror.
subtypes.Self-Worth Dependent on Weight: Judging whether one is a good or successful person solely based on weight or body shape.

S047.name: Compensatory_Behavior_NonPurging
S047.description: Recurrent inappropriate compensatory behaviors to prevent weight gain without purging (direct removal of food).

subtypes.Fasting: Intentionally stopping food intake for a certain period to prevent weight gain.
subtypes.Excessive Exercise: Repetitively performing exercise at a level that exceeds physical limits to prevent weight gain.

S049.name: Eating_Large_Amount
S049.description: Eating, in a discrete period of time, an amount of food that is definitely larger than what most individuals would eat in a similar period of time under similar circumstances.
examples: Eating more than 3-4 times the amount of a typical meal within 2 hours.
Continuously eating large amounts of high-calorie snacks in addition to main meals.
Eating enough to empty a significant portion of the refrigerator or pantry at once.
Eating clearly more food than others during the same period of time.

S050.name: Loss_of_Control
S050.description: A sense of lack of control over eating during the episode (e.g., a feeling that one cannot stop eating or control what or how much one is eating).
examples: A feeling that once I start eating, I cannot stop even if I want to.
Thinking 'I shouldn't eat any more' but mechanically continuing to eat.
A feeling of helplessness that I cannot decide for myself how much to eat.
Eating as if my body is being controlled by someone else.

symptom.disease_info: Bulimia Nervosa is characterized by recurrent binge-eating episodes with a sense of loss of control, followed by recurrent inappropriate compensatory behaviors intended to prevent weight gain. Self-evaluation is unduly influenced by body weight or shape, and the course often fluctuates with stress, secrecy, and periods of attempted dietary control. It is distinguished from binge-eating disorder by compensatory behaviors and from anorexia nervosa by the absence of persistently significantly low body weight as the defining feature.

patient.stressor: Martin’s closest community-theater friend, a fellow set designer who had also joined their walking club, died unexpectedly just as Martin was finishing a demanding civic design project. In the 4 months that followed, evenings once spent in the workshop or photographing bridges became solitary and disorganized, and Martin began having episodes of eating much larger amounts than intended, then trying to compensate with extended walks, skipped meals, or rigid next-day food rules rather than purging. The pattern became clinically significant when Martin noticed that judging their own worth had shifted from creative work and community contribution to a preoccupation with body size and whether they appeared disciplined. Martin sought psychiatric care after a grief-support facilitator heard them describe the eating cycle and suggested an evaluation with a clinician experienced in eating disorders.

S046.name: Body_Image_Weight_Shape_Disturbance
S046.description: Undue influence of body weight or shape on self-evaluation.
S046.manifestation: I used to judge my day by whether I solved a design problem or helped out at the theater, but lately I look at my stomach in the mirror and feel like the whole measure of me is whether I look controlled or sloppy.

S047.name: Compensatory_Behavior_NonPurging
S047.description: Recurrent inappropriate compensatory behaviors to prevent weight gain without purging (direct removal of food).
S047.manifestation: After a bad eating night, I’ll tell myself I’m making up for it by skipping breakfast and lunch or walking miles past my usual route, even when my knees are telling me I should head home.

S049.name: Eating_Large_Amount
S049.description: Eating, in a discrete period of time, an amount of food that is definitely larger than what most individuals would eat in a similar period of time under similar circumstances.
S049.manifestation: Some evenings I’ll start with leftovers and end up eating sandwiches, cereal, cookies, and whatever snack food is in the pantry, far more than I would ever put on a plate for a normal supper.

S050.name: Loss_of_Control
S050.description: A sense of lack of control over eating during the episode (e.g., a feeling that one cannot stop eating or control what or how much one is eating).
S050.manifestation: What brings me in is that once I start eating at night, it feels like I can see myself doing it and telling myself to stop, but my hands just keep going back for more.

add_requirements.The binge eating and inappropriate compe: For the last several months, most weeks have had at least one night where I eat like that and then spend the next day trying to make up for it by skipping meals, setting strict food rules, or taking an extra-long walk.
add_requirements.functional_impairment: I’m still managing my job and basic responsibilities, but I’ve been turning down theater and walking-club plans because I feel ashamed and preoccupied with whether I look disciplined enough.
add_requirements.duration: This has been going on for about 4 months, since my friend died and my evenings stopped feeling organized.
